record.paper_title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems
record.context_brief: representational time and origin of life
record.original_question: Does a distinct kind of representational time come into being with the origin or development of life, where living systems have representations of past and future states that enable memory, prediction, anticipation, learning, and action beyond immediate reaction in natural time?

evidence.quote:
Here, in contrast, we take a representational stance, and say that past and future exist as properties
of another kind of time, which we call representational time [33]. This representational time appears
along with the origin of life, as a necessary property of living systems 4. We stress that, despite its name,
representational time is not simply a representation of natural time: it is a new kind of time, one that
permits a view of the world that transcends what is possible with natural time, permitting agents to
form memories of the past, make predictions of possible futures, and act on these , rather than merely
react to the immediate.

Is there a new concept of time that comes into being with the origin/development
of life?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two notions of time. Natural time refers to the physical parameter governing the dynamics of inanimate processes, in which only the present instant is causally efficacious. Representational time refers to a hypothesized additional kind of time intrinsic to living systems, in which past and future states exist as internal representations within an agent, enabling memory of past states, prediction and anticipation of possible future states, learning, and goal-directed action that goes beyond immediate stimulus–response reaction.

Question: Does representational time, as defined above, come into being with the origin or development of life as a necessary property of living systems? Equivalently, is there a conceptually distinct kind of time — irreducible to natural time but rather constituted by the predictive and mnemonic representational capacities of organisms — that emerges with life and distinguishes living systems from non-living physical processes?

Provide a precise formulation of representational time, establish criteria under which a system can be said to possess it, and determine whether the emergence of life is necessary and/or sufficient for its existence.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is conceptual/philosophical, situated at the interface of theoretical biology, philosophy of time, and cognitive science. No definitive mathematical or scientific resolution exists; it remains an open foundational question.
